record.paper_title: Open questions for strongly interacting Fermi gases with zero-range interactions
record.original_question: Can the intrinsic phase diffusion and associated finite coherence time of an isolated finite-size pair condensate be experimentally verified in cold atomic gases? The setting is a finite, well-isolated superfluid in which phonon number fluctuations decorrelate through phonon collisions, producing a subextensive phase-diffusion coefficient Dλ proportional to 1/N rather than an externally imposed decoherence mechanism.

evidence.quote: At times long enough for a large number of collisions to have taken place, we therefore expect a diffusive spreading of the condensate phase, the variance of the random phase shift increasing linearly with time
There has been no experimental verification yet in cold atomic gases (the only quantum fluids sufficiently well isolated for the condensate loss of coherence to be intrinsic), even for bosons.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a finite, well-isolated superfluid of N paired fermions at zero (or very low) temperature, prepared as a pair condensate with a well-defined total particle number. In such a system, phonon number fluctuations decorrelate over time through phonon-phonon collisions, and standard theory predicts that the global condensate phase φ(t) undergoes diffusive spreading: for times long enough that many phonon collisions have occurred, the variance Var[φ(t) − φ(0)] grows linearly in t with a phase-diffusion coefficient D_λ. This coefficient is intrinsic (not due to coupling with an external bath) and is predicted to be subextensive, scaling as D_λ ∝ 1/N for fixed intensive parameters (density, temperature, interaction strength), so that the condensate has a finite intrinsic coherence time τ_c ∼ N/(intensive constant).

Problem: Devise and carry out an experiment in an ultracold atomic gas (the only known quantum fluid sufficiently isolated for the loss of condensate coherence to be of intrinsic origin) that directly measures the intrinsic phase-diffusion coefficient D_λ and the associated finite coherence time of an isolated finite-size pair condensate, and verifies the predicted 1/N scaling of D_λ together with the linear-in-time growth of the phase variance arising from phonon-collision-induced decorrelation of phonon number fluctuations. Equivalently, demonstrate experimentally that an isolated finite pair condensate loses coherence at the intrinsic rate predicted by this phonon-collision mechanism, rather than at a rate set by externally imposed decoherence.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches for experimental verification of intrinsic phonon-collision-induced phase diffusion with subextensive 1/N coefficient in isolated finite pair condensates return only theoretical predictions and unrelated double-well/quantum phase diffusion experiments. No experimental measurement of the intrinsic phase-diffusion coefficient and coherence time of an isolated pair condensate (or even bosonic condensate) of this kind appears in the literature as of 2026, indicating the problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: Universal dynamics of a pair condensate
status_evidence.snippet: Theoretical work on universal dynamics and phase diffusion of pair condensates; no experimental measurement of the intrinsic 1/N phase diffusion is reported.
status_evidence.claim: Recent theory continues to address phase diffusion in pair condensates without citing an experimental verification.

status_evidence.title: Phase and Phase Diffusion of a Split Bose-Einstein Condensate
status_evidence.snippet: Studies split/double-well condensates where phase diffusion is driven by number uncertainty, not the intrinsic phonon-collision mechanism of an isolated condensate.
status_evidence.claim: Existing phase-diffusion experiments target double-well/split condensates, not the intrinsic mechanism in a single isolated finite pair condensate.

status_evidence.title: Intrinsic dephasing in one-dimensional ultracold atom interferometers
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses 1D interferometer dephasing from bulk thermal fluctuations, distinct from subextensive 1/N phonon-collision phase diffusion in a 3D isolated pair condensate.
status_evidence.claim: Available intrinsic-dephasing experiments concern a different regime and do not verify the predicted 1/N pair-condensate phase diffusion.
